source: This local version follows the Norwegian Amerikaner rules checked against Norske kortspill. It supports three to six players with a standard deck and no jokers. To deal evenly, one, two or four twos are set aside for three, five or six players; four players use all 52 cards. The player left of the dealer bids first. A regular bid must be at least half your hand rounded up and higher than the current bid; you may also pass or call Amerikaner to try every trick alone without a partner or trump. If you win a regular bid, lead the first card to set trump and request an in-play card in that suit that is not in your hand. Its holder must play it in the first trick and becomes your partner. If no matching card remains in opponents’ hands on a later lead, continue without a partner; only the declarer is scored as the bidder. Players must follow the led suit when possible. Highest trump wins a trick, or the highest card in the led suit if there is no trump. The declarer and partner each gain the bid when they make it, or each lose the bid when they miss; other players gain one point for each trick they take. A successful Amerikaner earns 52 points and a failed one loses 52. After a round, the dealer moves left. Once a score reaches 52, the highest score wins. Local computer opponents make simple heuristic choices; there is no online multiplayer.
